responseFields.description: Upstream's own verdict on whether this profile is finished. Passed through rather than interpreted: clients decide what they do with it. Absent when upstream did not report it, which is distinct from `false` -- "not answered" must not read as "answered no".

responseFields.name: profileId
responseFields.description: The legacy `user_profile` row's id, stringified -- including `"0"`, which means no row exists yet. A caller uses this to decide whether completing the profile must go through the create step (`POST /me/profile`) first, or can go straight to the edit step (`PATCH /me/profile`). Passed through rather than interpreted, same as `isProfileComplete` above: `"0"` is a real value, not an absent one, so it is never dropped by a falsy check.

operations.title: List the owner’s contacts
operations.description: Supports search, sort, a sharing filter and a relationship filter. Note: supplying `q` disables sorting, because the upstream search variant accepts no sort parameters.

responseFields.name: id
responseFields.description: Opaque contact identifier. On the legacy path this is the backend's integer `network_id` rendered as a string. On the new path it will be a `public_id` UUID. The field name and type do not change at cutover, but **the value does** — see the open question in `docs/migration/implementation-status.md`.

responseFields.name: hasAccount
responseFields.description: Whether this contact resolves to an account that can sign in.

responseFields.name: userId
responseFields.description: **The contact's own** account id, when they have one — not `id` above, which identifies the caller's record *of* them, and not `ownerUserId` below, which is the caller. Absent for a contact with no account; the upstream's `0` sentinel is dropped rather than passed on, so a present value is always a real id. It is what lets a caller match a contact to a story's `ownerId` and so answer "which of my contacts wrote this". Without it, a reader on another member's story cannot find their own contact record for that member, and every surface that needs one — commenting through it, or asking to keep the story — has nothing to address.

responseFields.name: profileUrl
responseFields.description: Path to the contact's profile page, e.g. `/user/senthil-kumar-mhf8drco71`. Absent when there is nothing to show — the contact has no account, or has not shared one with this member.

responseFields.name: accessLevel
responseFields.description: Who may see this contact on the owner's surfaces.

responseFields.name: ownerUserId
responseFields.description: The id of the member whose address book this row is in — the **caller**, not the contact. It is therefore identical on every row. It is here because this is the only list a member can read that reports their own user id: `/api/v1/me` carries none, and a story read carries its owner's. Some upstream writes — copying a story onto your own timeline — demand that id and refuse to infer it from the session, and a caller with no other way to learn it cannot make the call at all. Repeated per row rather than lifted into `meta` because that is how the upstream sends it, and this layer does not reshape what it is given.

responseFields.name: createdAt
responseFields.description: ISO-8601 UTC, or absent.

fields.name: email
fields.description: Not unique, and deliberately not validated as if it were. The same address legitimately appears on contacts owned by different people, and the legacy data contains one address on two contacts under different names in different scripts. Identity resolution is the new backend's job, done against `person_contact_points`.

fields.name: relationship
fields.description: The relationship label. A free string, capped. Deliberately not an enum: the legacy API exposes three mutually inconsistent vocabularies for this field — a 12-value write list, an observed set with case collisions (`Other` and `other`), and a 22-value filter list including `Step Granddaughter`. Constraining to any one of them would reject values the current client sends. The new schema models this as a `relationship_types` lookup, and the mapping happens at migration.

fields.name: dateOfDeath
fields.description: Absent means living. `0` is not an accepted input.

fields.name: guardian
fields.description: Required when `isMinor` is true. `@ValidateIf` returning false skips every other decorator on the property, which is what makes the requirement conditional rather than absolute.

fields.name: recipientUserId
fields.description: The recipient's own account id — required for the emailed sign-in link to reach the right account, per the legacy frontend's own note on this step. Kept as a numeric string, not `number`: the mapper immediately `String(...)`s it for the legacy call anyway, and combining `@BlankToUndefined()` with `@Type(() => Number)` on one property is order-sensitive in a way that silently turns a blank submission into `0` rather than `undefined` — `@Type`'s coercion runs before the blank check, converting `''` to `0` first. Matches `ProfileFieldsDto.raceId`'s own reasoning for staying a string despite being numeric underneath.

fields.name: authorUserId
fields.description: The signed-in member's own account id. Same string reasoning as `recipientUserId`.

operations.title: Resolve a shared story link
operations.description: Turns the `story` token from an invitation e-mail into the story it addresses, and signs the visitor in when the backend grants a session — which it does, so someone with no account can read the story. Answers 404 when the link no longer resolves, which is what an expired or tampered token looks like.

responseFields.name: entityContributionId
responseFields.description: The contribution the link was generated from, when it came from one.

responseFields.name: auth
responseFields.description: The session the link granted. Absent when the backend minted none — a caller must check rather than assume, the same as on the other two link types.

responseFields.name: entityId
responseFields.description: The story or profile the link addresses. Required: a link that resolves to no entity has not resolved, and the mapper answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` rather than returning a shell.

fields.name: story
fields.description: The `story` query parameter, exactly as it appeared in the URL.

operations.title: Resolve a collaboration invitation link
operations.description: Turns the `contributor` and `code` tokens into the invitation they name, and signs the invitee in when the backend grants a session. `outcome` comes from the backend, never from `stage`: the same invitation issues different tokens for commenting and declining, and both arrive as `stage=invite`.

responseFields.name: networkId
responseFields.description: The relationship row between the two accounts.

responseFields.name: outcome
responseFields.description: What the link resolved to: `approved` and `rejected` are the values seen in real responses. Deliberately a `string` rather than a union. The backend's full vocabulary is not documented anywhere, and a union here would silently drop a value it had not been told about — which, for a field that says whether an invitation was accepted, is the worst possible failure. Narrow it once the set is confirmed.

responseFields.name: auth
responseFields.description: The session the link granted. Absent when the backend minted none, which is a legitimate answer — a link that only reports an outcome does not need to sign anybody in. A caller must check for it rather than assume it.

responseFields.name: entityId
responseFields.description: The story or profile the link addresses. Required: a link that resolves to no entity has not resolved, and the mapper answers `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` rather than returning a shell.

fields.name: stage
fields.description: Which point of the journey the link was sent from. `invite` is the only value observed; it is forwarded rather than interpreted.
